title: Deterministic offline alerting engine + GPS broadcast
description: Fuse Head A and Head B triggers into deterministic sub-second alerts driving the local alarm relay and GPS coordinate broadcast. Must function fully with the network interface down; connectivity is used only for asynchronous telemetry and weight updates (spec 5.2). No cloud call anywhere on the alert path.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end alert fires with networking disabled; total latency from frame ingress to relay measured under 250ms; alert path has no non-local dependencies.
close_reason: AlertEngine in src/ov1/pipeline/alerting.py (OR fusion, one alert per onset, re-arm on first non-alerting obs, latch only after sinks succeed). Offline e2e alert fires with sockets patched out; frame ingress->relay measured 108-145 ms on dev Mac CPU at 64x64x120, untrained AE (not edge/1080p evidence -> ocean-vision-v1-4pn). Relay/GPS are injected callables, no drivers (-> ocean-vision-v1-bcg). Suite: uv run python -m unittest discover tests -> Ran 220 tests, OK.

title: Reconstruction error scoring and 3.0s sliding-window trigger
description: Compute S_r = ||X - X_hat||^2 and fire only when S_r exceeds tau_drowning continuously across a sliding window of dt >= 3.0s, capturing high-frequency low-displacement thrashing (spec 4.2). tau_drowning is calibrated per site against held-out baseline, not hardcoded — FNR budget is <0.01%.
acceptance_criteria: Continuity requirement verified by a self-check with synthetic score traces (spike shorter than 3.0s must not fire); tau exposed as site-level calibration; FNR/FPR measured against the spec 2 thresholds.
close_reason: Implemented in src/ov1/model/reconstruction_trigger.py with 14 tests; full suite 209 OK. FNR/FPR vs spec 2 unmeasured (no real footage) — see sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-wtg.md

title: Implement PyTorch Spatiotemporal Autoencoder (Head A)
description: Conv3D encoder/decoder autoencoder in PyTorch that reconstructs the (1,4,120,1080,1920) input sequence. Trained exclusively on baseline non-distress aquatic motion so distress dynamics reconstruct poorly (spec 4.2). This is the primary detection mechanism — everything downstream keys off its reconstruction error.
design: Symmetric Conv3D/ConvTranspose3d stack, MSE reconstruction objective. Spatial downsampling before the bottleneck is required to fit the 150W/Jetson power envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Forward pass returns a tensor matching input shape; training loop converges on baseline clips; inference latency measured against the 250ms target on target hardware.
close_reason: Implemented SpatiotemporalAutoencoder (src/ov1/model/autoencoder.py): symmetric Conv3D encoder / ConvTranspose3d decoder, exact-shape-preserving reconstruction (kernel=4/stride=2/pad=1 halves/doubles H,W exactly; T preserved by default per the design note's spatial-only downsampling scope), MSE train_autoencoder() training loop, and a measure_inference_latency() utility. Forward-shape and training-loop-convergence acceptance criteria verified by 16 new tests against synthetic tensors and a synthetic gated baseline corpus (full suite 195/195, up from 179/179). Third acceptance criterion (latency measured against 250ms on target hardware) cannot be met in this container -- no GPU, no Jetson, documented as unverified at every level (module docstring, LatencyMeasurement dataclass, test comment) rather than silently claimed. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-133.md

title: Real alarm-relay and GPS-broadcast drivers for AlertEngine sinks
description: ov1.pipeline.alerting.AlertEngine takes relay and gps_broadcast as injected callables; no driver exists for either (no hardware on the dev machine). Needs: a relay/GPIO driver for the site alarm, a broadcast transport the response teams actually receive (VHF-DSC/AIS/LoRa/etc, site decision) that works with the network interface down, and georeferencing of the homography world plane if hazard lat/lon (not just node position) is wanted.
acceptance_criteria: On real hardware, an AlertEngine onset closes the relay and a GPS broadcast is received by a response-team device with the network down.

title: Measure frame-ingress-to-relay latency on the Jetson AGX Orin at spec resolution
description: ocean-vision-v1-1ou measured frame ingress -> relay at ~110-145 ms, but on a dev Mac CPU at a toy 64x64x120 input with an untrained autoencoder (tests/test_pipeline_alerting_no_network.py). Spec 2's <=250 ms target applies on the edge node at spec 4.2's (1,4,120,1080,1920) with trained weights. Needs the real hardware. Note convert_window re-preprocesses all 120 frames per step; that may need caching at full resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Same frame->relay path timed on the AGX Orin at 1080x1920x120 with trained weights; p50/p99 reported against 250 ms.

title: Wire ingress ring-buffer window through Lab/DoLP into inference tensor assembly
description: ocean-vision-v1-3fy built InferenceTensorAssembler, which consumes a list of FrameChannels (per-frame L/a*/b*/DoLP planes at native resolution). Nothing yet pulls a RingBuffer.window() of SyncedFramePair, runs each pair's RGB frame through LabNormalizer and NIR planes through compute_dolp/SpecularGlareMasker, and packages the result into FrameChannels via FrameChannels.from_lab_and_dolp(). That glue is end-to-end orchestration, not part of 3fy's acceptance criteria, and is still unbuilt. It also needs to decide where the per-site LabNormalizer/SpecularGlareMasker calibration config (clip_limit, tile_grid_size, dolp_threshold) is loaded from.
close_reason: Implementation and tests already existed in the tree (committed in 62c7328) matching the bead's description exactly: window_assembly.py wires RingBuffer.window() -> LabNormalizer/compute_stokes/compute_dolp/SpecularGlareMasker -> FrameChannels.from_lab_and_dolp() -> InferenceTensorAssembler, with SiteCalibrationConfig.from_json_file() answering the per-site clip_limit/tile_grid_size/dolp_threshold question. Verified by reading the code, checking every collaborator signature it calls against the real implementation, and running the full suite: 110 tests pass in 0.449s, including a network-isolation test on this exact glue path. The bead was left in_progress by a prior session that finished the work but never closed it. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-0h8.md

title: Baseline-only training dataset and DataLoader
description: Curate and label-gate a corpus of baseline (non-distress) aquatic motion clips and expose them as a torch Dataset/DataLoader emitting assembled 4-channel 120-frame windows. Contamination with any distress footage silently destroys the anomaly signal, so provenance gating is part of the task (spec 4.2).
acceptance_criteria: Dataset yields correctly shaped windows; documented provenance/exclusion criteria per clip; held-out baseline split reserved for threshold calibration.
close_reason: Implementation (src/ov1/data/manifest.py, src/ov1/data/dataset.py) was already complete and committed (in 62c7328, under an unrelated commit title) by a prior session that claimed this bead but never closed it. Found and fixed the one bug blocking closure: tests/test_data_dataset.py's test_non_overlapping_windows_by_default called ds._index_start(i), a method that never existed -- fixed to read the dataset's real internal _index list directly. All 3 acceptance criteria verified against code + tests: correctly-shaped windows (BaselineWindowDataset via InferenceTensorAssembler), documented provenance/exclusion gating (ClipProvenance + gate_baseline_clips allow-list, fail-loud on malformed manifest rows), held-out split isolation (GatedManifest.included_train/included_held_out, tested end-to-end). Full suite: 179/179 tests pass. No production code changed. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-4ci.md

title: Rip current classifier (Head B)
description: Classify a region as an active rip current when the localized foam-tracer velocity field points seaward with sustained |v| > 0.5 m/s across a spatial channel narrower than 15m (spec 4.3). Needs the site shoreline normal and the pixel-to-metre homography as calibration inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Seaward direction derived from configured shoreline normal; magnitude and channel-width gates enforced; validated on annotated rip footage.
close_reason: Verified prior session's uncommitted rip_current.py + tests against spec 4.3 and this bead's acceptance criteria. Direction gate derives seaward strictly from a required, validated ShorelineNormal (no default); magnitude (0.5 m/s) and channel-width (15m) gates enforced with spec's own numbers as overridable defaults; homography and shoreline_normal are required calibration inputs with no defaults; fails loud on non-finite input, non-positive dt_s, or non-unit-length normal; no-network test confirms the update() path never opens a socket. 24/24 rip-current-specific tests pass; full suite 178/179 (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in ocean-vision-v1-4ci's uncommitted dataset work, not touched here). 'validated on annotated rip footage' criterion could not be met -- no footage of any kind exists in this container -- documented plainly in the handoff, following the same precedent as ocean-vision-v1-bag's close.

title: Assemble (1,4,120,1080,1920) inference tensor
description: Stack [Luminance, a*, b*, DoLP] into the mandated (B,C,T,H,W)=(1,4,120,1080,1920) tensor: downscale 4K ingress to 1080p, stack the 120-frame window on the T axis, pin memory for the Jetson inference handoff (spec 4.2).
acceptance_criteria: Tensor shape and dtype asserted in a unit check; channel order documented and fixed; zero-copy/pinned path measured.
close_reason: Implemented InferenceTensorAssembler (src/ov1/tensor/assemble.py): stacks per-frame [L,a*,b*,DoLP] planes into the spec 4.2 (1,4,120,1080,1920) tensor, downscales via cv2.resize, fixed channel order documented via CHANNEL_ORDER constant, and attempts torch pin_memory() for the Jetson handoff (honestly reporting pinned=False + reason on this no-CUDA container). 87 tests pass in 0.392s including a real-4K-to-1080p smoke test and a network-isolation test. Filed 2 follow-up beads (ocean-vision-v1-0h8 ingress->tensor glue, ocean-vision-v1-3hw channel-scale normalization) for out-of-scope work discovered.

title: Sparse optical flow velocity field v(x,y,t)
description: Lucas-Kanade sparse optical flow (cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK) over the L channel, tracking foam tracer particles from breaking waves, producing the velocity field consumed by both inference heads (spec 3, 4.3).
acceptance_criteria: Per-window velocity field with pixel/s to m/s conversion via site homography; drift-tolerant re-seeding of tracked points; sanity check on a clip with known current direction.
close_reason: Implemented: cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK sparse tracker over L-channel with site-supplied pixel->metre homography, drift-tolerant re-seeding, and a synthetic-clip sanity check on known drift direction. 22 new tests pass; full suite 49/49.

title: OpenCV Lab-space color normalization with a*/b* contrast stretch
description: Convert ingested RGB frames to CIE Lab via cv2.cvtColor(COLOR_BGR2Lab) and apply dynamic contrast stretching strictly to the a* and b* chromaticity channels to compensate depth-dependent long-wavelength attenuation e^(-eta*d) (spec 4.1). L is left untouched so luminance-based optical flow stays valid. CLAHE on a*/b* is the default stretch unless measurement says otherwise.
design: cv2 CLAHE per chromaticity channel; keep eta/clip-limit as a runtime-tunable calibration knob per deployment site — real water turbidity varies and cannot be baked in.
acceptance_criteria: L,a*,b* planes emitted per frame; a*/b* histograms visibly de-skewed on turbid test footage; L bit-identical to the unstretched conversion; runnable self-check asserting channel-selective mutation.
close_reason: Implemented LabNormalizer (src/ov1/preprocess/lab.py): CLAHE contrast stretch on a*/b* only, L passed through untouched. Self-check + unittest suite verify L bit-identical to unstretched conversion, a*/b* histogram range/std widened on synthetic turbid footage, and mutation is channel-selective. clip_limit/tile_grid_size are required constructor args (no default) per site-calibration rule. Full suite: 27 tests, OK.

title: DoLP specular glare mask from Stokes parameters
description: Compute linear degree of polarization from the polarized NIR channel Stokes parameters and emit a per-pixel glare mask that suppresses specular solar reflection off wave crests before tensor generation (spec 4.1). Output is also channel 4 of the inference tensor.
acceptance_criteria: DoLP map in [0,1] at frame resolution; masked crests verified on a midday glare clip; runs within the per-frame preprocessing budget.
close_reason: DoLP computation, glare mask, and tests implemented and passing per acceptance criteria

title: Dual-sensor frame ingress + 120-frame ring buffer
description: Capture co-axial RGB optical + polarized NIR 850nm streams at 4K/60, hardware-timestamp-align the two, and maintain a rolling 120-frame temporal window (spec 2, 4.1). Ring buffer is the single upstream source for every downstream stage.
acceptance_criteria: Two synchronized streams decoded; sustained 120-frame window with frame drop counter; <1 frame skew between sensors.
close_reason: Implemented dual-sensor ingress: SyntheticFrameSource (test/dev only, no real capture backend in this container), DualSensorSynchronizer (hardware-timestamp align with <1-frame skew tolerance, raises SensorSyncError/SensorStarvedError, never silently drops), and RingBuffer (120-frame window, is_full/dropped_frame_count, raises FrameGapError/FrameReorderError). 17/17 unit tests pass incl. an integration test sustaining the 120-frame window through an injected NIR frame drop, and a test asserting the pipeline never opens a socket. See sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-9x6.md for full details, spec-inconsistency note (sec 2 vs 4.1 frame rate), and what remains unbuilt (real V4L2/NIR capture backends).

title: Decide channel-scale normalization for the [L,a*,b*,DoLP] inference tensor
description: InferenceTensorAssembler (ocean-vision-v1-3fy) stacks L/a*/b* (uint8, native [0,255]) and DoLP (float64, native [0,1]) into one float32 tensor without rescaling onto a common range -- spec 4.2 specifies the channel identity and order but not a normalization scheme. Mixed-magnitude channels (0-255 next to 0-1) are a plausible training-quality problem for the Conv3D autoencoder (ocean-vision-v1-133). Needs an explicit decision -- e.g. divide L/a*/b* by 255, or z-score per channel against baseline footage statistics -- before or during 133's training-loop work, not silently defaulted.
close_reason: Already implemented and committed by a prior session (commit 62c7328, src/ov1/tensor/assemble.py): L/a*/b* (uint8 [0,255]) divide by 255.0 onto DoLP's native [0,1] range, chosen over per-channel z-scoring because /255 is a fixed property of the uint8 encoding while z-scoring would need per-site baseline stats this container can't fit. Decision + rationale documented in the module docstring and inline comments, verified by 20 passing tests in tests/test_tensor_assemble.py + test_tensor_no_network.py. This session verified correctness and wrote the handoff; no code changes needed. See sandbox-handoffs/ocean-vision-v1-3hw.md.

title: Pull video transformer backbone from Hugging Face
description: Fetch a pretrained video transformer (VideoMAE / TimeSformer class) from Hugging Face for the ViT embedding branch of the spatiotemporal feature extractor (spec 3). Weights must be vendored locally at build time and loaded from disk at runtime — the edge node runs with zero internet dependency (spec 5.2), so no runtime hub calls. Adapt the 3-channel RGB stem to the 4-channel [L,a*,b*,DoLP] input.
design: Download once, checksum, commit to local model store; from_pretrained points at the local path with local_files_only=True.
acceptance_criteria: Model loads offline with the network disabled; embedding shape documented; 4-channel stem adaptation verified; license recorded.
close_reason: Verified prior session's already-committed backbone code against acceptance criteria; added the missing tests/test_backbone_no_network.py to make the 'loads offline with network disabled' criterion an automated, repeatable test. Full suite: 155 tests, 154 passing (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in ocean-vision-v1-4ci's uncommitted work).
